learningObjective: Distinguish the state that changes after every micro-batch (the gradient buffer) from the parameters that change only once after K micro-batches.
mediumRationale: A deterministic SVG timeline is the smallest medium that can align four micro-batches, the progressively accumulated gradient expression, an unchanged parameter value, and one optimizer-step boundary. The fixed K = 4 example makes both the averaging arithmetic and state transition visible without adding controls or reproducing a source figure.

mediumComparison.mermaid: Rejected because automatic graph layout would obscure the regular timing and exact one-quarter gradient arithmetic that the lesson depends on.
mediumComparison.svg: Selected because a fixed timeline can align each backward pass with the gradient-buffer contents and show exactly one parameter update; established vector primitives provide theme and print behavior.
mediumComparison.semanticHtml: Rejected because a table could enumerate the four states but would make the temporal flow and single update boundary less immediate.
mediumComparison.interaction: Rejected because varying K adds controls without changing the core invariant; a static K = 4 example is sufficient and remains useful without JavaScript.
mediumComparison.paperReuse: Rejected because the reviewed official documentation explains the mechanism in prose and code rather than providing a narrowly reusable state timeline; no external figure is needed, and no artwork reuse permission was assumed.
mediumComparison.noVisual: Rejected because the prose loop does not spatially separate two simultaneous facts: `.grad` changes after each backward call while the model parameters remain fixed until the accumulation boundary.

pages.insight: The character-language-model training loop shows the conventional per-batch sequence zero_grad, backward, and optimizer.step, providing the baseline that accumulation changes.
The mixed-precision slide explicitly places gradient conversion and unscaling before the optimizer step, reinforcing that gradients can be prepared separately from applying the parameter update.
The training-stack slide explicitly names gradient accumulation as the technique used to reach large effective batch sizes, but it gives no mechanism, timing, or averaging visual.

deckReview.notes: The complete 214-page local deck was text-indexed for accumulation, batches, mini-batches, backward passes, gradient buffers, zero_grad, optimizer steps, and training loops. Pages 96-98 were inspected around the conventional loop on page 97: page 96 is word2vec preprocessing and page 98 is tokenization. Pages 113-116 were inspected around the only explicit gradient-accumulation mention: page 113 is speculative decoding, page 114 is mixed precision, page 115 lists the modern training stack, and page 116 begins speech re-scoring. No slide shows multiple backward passes feeding one optimizer step, and no deck artwork or layout is reused.

sources.title: PyTorch Tensor.backward documentation
sources.usage: Verified that backward accumulates gradients into leaf tensors and that callers must zero or clear .grad when a fresh accumulation window is required.
sources.license: No documentation wording, source code, or imagery is copied. The implementation uses only the documented API semantics and is an original schematic, so documentation-figure reuse rights are not relied upon.

sources.title: PyTorch Zeroing out gradients recipe
sources.usage: Verified the official explanation that repeated backward calls add to gradient buffers rather than overwrite them and that zeroing defines the next gradient window.
sources.license: No recipe prose, code, data, or imagery is copied. The original state timeline cites the behavior rather than adapting any source material.

sources.title: Hugging Face Accelerate gradient accumulation guide
sources.usage: Cross-checked the standard K-step loop, loss division by K, single optimizer step, and distributed synchronization caveat against maintained framework documentation.
sources.license: The guide is used as an authoritative technical reference only. No code, wording, examples, or figures are reproduced, and no broad reuse grant is assumed from public access.

sourceReview.notes: The hardest prose-only model is not the effective-batch formula but the two different state clocks inside one accumulation window: each backward call adds a normalized micro-batch gradient to `.grad`, while every forward pass still reads the same parameter value; only the boundary call to optimizer.step consumes the completed average and creates the next parameter value. The visual uses an illustrative K = 4 window with equal-sized micro-batches and mean-reduced losses. Its geometry, labels, arithmetic, and composition are original and do not adapt a deck or documentation figure.

agentReview.summary: Read the complete article, searched all 214 deck pages and inspected both relevant neighborhoods, then checked maintained PyTorch and Hugging Face documentation before selecting an original state timeline.

implementation.accessibility: The SVG title and description state the complete K = 4 sequence, including unchanged parameters, the four gradient-buffer expressions, and the sole optimizer update. Step numbers, repeated theta labels, arithmetic, a dashed accumulation path, and a solid update arrow carry the meaning without color. The established horizontally scrollable vector primitive keeps a 42rem canvas legible at 390 CSS pixels, uses theme variables in dark mode, and removes its minimum width under the existing print rules.
